verifications.claim: Comcast has agreed to a $117.5 million class-action settlement.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Comcast has reached a $117.5 million settlement" (R1); "Comcast's $117.5 million settlement" (R2); "Comcast agreed to pay $117.5 million" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Comcast agreed to exactly $117.5 million class-action settlement.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "after a major data breach... in October 2023" (R1); "stemmed from a data breach in October 2023" (R2); "2023 hack" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources link the settlement directly to the 2023 data breach/cyberattack.

verifications.claim: The cyberattack exposed the personal data of approximately 30 million Xfinity customers.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "more than 35 million customers" (R1); "More than 30 million people... eligible" (R2); "36 million Xfinity customers" (R3); "35.8 million customers" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources support exposure of personal data to 30+ million (35-36M specified), but claim's 'approximately 30 million' is less precise than exact figures provided.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "in October 2023" (R1); "data breach in October 2023" (R2); "late October 2023" (R3); "between Oct. 16, 2023 and Oct. 19, 2023" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly confirm the cyberattack occurred in October 2023.

verifications.claim: Individuals eligible for the settlement are those notified by Xfinity that their personal information was compromised in the October 2023 breach.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "notified in December 2023 that your data may have been compromised in the aforementioned breach" (R1); "received breach notification from the company in December 2023" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely describe eligibility as those notified by Comcast/Xfinity about compromise in the October 2023 breach.

verifications.claim: Eligible customers can receive up to $10,000 in reimbursement for documented out-of-pocket losses.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Lost time and expenses settlement payments are capped at $10,000" (R1); "claim up to $10,000" (R2); "Up to $10,000 to People Affected" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state up to $10,000 for documented out-of-pocket losses.

verifications.claim: Eligible customers can receive up to $150 for lost time ($30 per hour for up to 5 hours).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "$30 per hour for up to five hours of lost time" (R1); "$30 an hour up to five hours" (R2); "up to five hours of lost time at $30 per hour" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources exactly match $30/hour for up to 5 hours (=$150) for lost time.

verifications.claim: Eligible customers can receive a $50 flat cash payment if they did not experience direct out-of-pocket losses.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "alternative payment of up to $50" (R1); "estimated $50 payout" (R2); "Alternative Cash Payment, estimated in the amount of $50" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm $50 (or up to/estimated $50, pro rata) alternative payment for those without documented losses.

verifications.claim: Eligible customers can receive three years of free identity defense and restoration services.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "three years of credit monitoring services" (R4); "three years of identity protection services" (R6); "three years of identity defense services" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state three years of free identity protection/defense/restoration services.

verifications.claim: Claims must be submitted by August 14, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "by August 14, 2026" (R1); "All claims must be filed by Aug. 14" (R2); "by Aug. 14" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources specify exact claim submission deadline as August 14, 2026.

verifications.claim: A final approval hearing is scheduled for July 7, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "final approval hearing is scheduled for July 7, 2026" (R1); "final hearing is scheduled on July 7" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm final approval hearing on July 7, 2026.

verifications.claim: Customers who do not submit a claim or opt out remain part of the class.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "choose to do nothing, meaning they will not get compensated but also give up the right to sue" (R1); "Customers who do nothing will remain part of the settlement class" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources state that not acting (no claim, no opt-out) keeps customers in the class.

verifications.claim: Such customers will not receive a cash payment.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated for customers who do nothing.

verifications.claim: Such customers may still enroll in the free identity protection services.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "but will still be able to enroll in the identity protection services once the settlement is finalized" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated that non-claimants who remain in class can still enroll in services.

verifications.claim: The lawsuit alleges Comcast failed to secure customer data.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "accused Comcast of failing to protect sensitive data" (R1); "failed to protect sensitive user data" (R2); "did not have adequate cybersecurity mechanisms" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe lawsuit alleging failure to secure/protect customer data.

verifications.claim: Comcast has denied the allegation that it failed to secure customer data.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The company has denied any wrongdoing" (R1); "Comcast denies wrongdoing" (R2); "Comcast denied any wrongdoing" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources uniformly state Comcast denies wrongdoing/allegations.
